thread:
ops-oncall: Heads up — we are seeing a spike of 503s in eu-west-1 starting ~09:12 UTC. Impacting inference frontends. I'm putting today's release slot for release/23.4.1 on HOLD until we understand root cause. Incident INC-2026.

deploy-bot: Deployment 23.4.1 (canary -> eu-west-1) scheduled at 2024-07-12T10:00Z has been PAUSED by ops-oncall. Reason: Incident INC-2026.

matt.r: Copy. Thanks for the quick flag. I'll stop the canary rollout and mark the job as blocked. matt.r is taking ownership of release gating.

jen.p: Ok — I'll update the release notes to note the hold and add a short blurb for customers who check the changelog. Also pinging support for external comms. :loudspeaker:

support-lead: On it. I'll draft a brief status blurb for support channels: "Scheduled update delayed due to regional availability issues; monitoring." Want me to include an ETA placeholder?

ops-oncall: No ETA yet. We suspect a KV cache eviction cascade after a recent infra autoscaling event. Deepak is running a quick hypothesis test.

deepak: Reproduced a small cache-thundering pattern in staging with a scaled-down load runner. Patch idea: staggered warmed-up nodes + short TTL on the prefix cache. Testing patch now. If patch looks good, we can do a targeted hotfix to control plane config so release can remain blocked but not roll forward.

leo: For gating: should we pin the control-plane binary to v23.4.0-hotfix before we attempt any resume? If we don't pin, deploy automation may roll forward to the canary change that triggered the issue.

release-manager: Agreed — pin control-plane to v23.4.0-hotfix for any resumed canaries. Also we should move the scheduled main rollout out of today's change window. Propose: shift by 24 hours and re-run canary once internal postmortem gives go/no-go.

jen.p: That works. I'll edit the release calendar and note the deferred window + pinned version. Add: update release notes to include the temporary pin and rationale.

deploy-bot: Action recorded: "pin control-plane -> v23.4.0-hotfix" (requested by release-manager). Canary job remains paused. Scheduled rollout for 2024-07-12T10:00Z has been moved to 2024-07-13T10:00Z (tentative).

matt.r: For rollback decision: do we want an automatic rollback if errors exceed 1% for 5m during canary resume, or manual rollback? I lean auto with page to oncall + release-manager.

ops-oncall: Auto rollback + page is fine. We need to avoid noisy flaps; set cooldown to 10m between roll attempts.

support-lead: I'll prepare an internal explainer for SRE + sales so folks know the reschedule and the pin. Want a one-liner for customer-facing copy: "We delayed the scheduled update in EU while we investigate elevated 503s. No customer data was affected."

deepak: Patch validated on staging load. Staggered warmup + reduced prefix TTL removed the cache cascade in our run. Plan: apply hotfix to a single control-plane instance in eu-west-1, rerun a confined canary, watch for 15m. If stable, expand.

jen.p: Timelines — can we target a confined canary run in 45–60 minutes from now? If not, we'll keep the 24h shift.

ops-oncall: 45m looks doable. We'll keep the slot blocked for now. When we start the confined canary, I'll post updates here.

release-manager: I'll update the release ticket with decisions: hold, pin to v23.4.0-hotfix, tentative reschedule + guarded canary with auto-rollback. Assign follow-ups: deepak (hotfix), matt.r (canary gating), support-lead (customer messaging).

deploy-bot: Note: when the canary resumes it will run with the pinned artifact. Auto-rollback policy set to 1% error for 5m with 10m cooldown.

matt.r: Thanks all. Quick checklist for the canary resume posted in the release ticket: roll hotfix -> start single-zone canary -> monitor latency/error dashboards -> expand if stable -> unpin when clean.

ops-oncall: Closing this thread for now while we run the patch. Will re-open with the canary start time. :white_check_mark:

support-lead: Thanks team. I'll hold off on external comms until you confirm canary results.

(automated) incident-bot: INC-2026 status updated -> investigating.
